newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Recount confirms Izetbegovic tops presidency.
newsitem.headline: Recount confirms Izetbegovic tops presidency.

text.p: A recount of votes in Bosnia's elections confirmed that President Alija Izetbegovic won the top job in a new collective presidency, international organisers said on Sunday.

But the "preliminary final result" showing Izetbegovic narrowly beating Serb separatist Momcilo Krajisnik must still be re-verified by computer and opened to possible appeals before it can be officially certified, a process likely to take until next weekend, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe added.

The OSCE said on Saturday that many errors in the vote count had forced a recount and cross-check of margins in key races including the presidency, where a "provisional" victory by Izetbegovic had been announced last week.

Preliminary final results released on Sunday showed Izetbegovic, a Moslem, finishing with 731,024 votes to 690,130 for Krajisnik, ultra-nationalist speaker of parliament in Bosnia's separatist Serb entity.

The Croat seat on the tripartite presidency was taken by Kresimir Zubak with 329,891 votes. Sunday's results confirmed provisional totals released last week with a slight widening of Izetbegovic's margin over Krajisnik.

"The first round of tabulation and reconciliation of the results has been completed for the presidential contest. Mr Izetbegovic has come out on top as was speculated all week," said Jeff Fischer, elections director in the Bosnia mission of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
